why: Expression cycle 14 (docs/v3/cycles/expression-14.md) lost points to four kit gaps that need a public field, so they cannot ride in a behaviour row: two cards in one row end at different heights (n64 .16: 611 against 635 px; n65 .25: 7 px and a blank band under row 12; n63's fixed wrappers leave a dead band), stacked panes inside one ChartCard cannot share its box (n63 .7, markers in n63 and n67: a nested `height="fill"` draws 320 px and ignores its parent, so both builders hard-coded pixel heights), a long numeric table has no phone form between 1,500 px of cards and a sideways scroll (n65 .23 K5; cycle 13's n62 windows table scrolled sideways at 390 too), and `useFormat` has no duration in words, no day-and-month date and no tick format apart from the readout's (n66 .29 F6 '12:29:51' read as a clock; wishes in n63, n64 and n66).
what: A Spec, then the fields it rules on: one height for the cards of a row, panes that share a card's box, a phone form for a long numeric table, and three formats.
owns: packages/basalt-ui/src/charts/** including charts/contract.ts where the Spec rules a field
packages/basalt-ui/src/cards/** including cards/contract.ts where the Spec rules a field
packages/basalt-ui/src/table/** including table/contract.ts where the Spec rules a field
packages/basalt-ui/src/core/format* where the Spec rules a format
packages/basalt-ui/docs/** and agent references generated from them
their tests and the playground's kit pages that show them
change: Write a one-page Spec first, then build what it rules. (1) Cards and panels in one row end at one height: a ChartCard beside a DataPanel or StatCard in one grid row stretches to the row or declares a shared height, with a rows body that fills rather than reserves (n64 .16, n65 .25, n63's dead band). (2) Panes that share a card's box: a ChartCard that stacks two or three charts on one x (the two-pane recipe) hands each pane its share of `box.height`, or a pane group takes weights, so no app hard-codes pixel heights per size class (n63 .7; n67 marker; the two-pane recipe's equal-rows grid did not help either builder). (3) A phone form for a long numeric table: between `phone: 'cards'` (12 cards, about 1,500 px on n65) and `phone: 'scroll'` (the answer column off screen), a form that keeps the name, the answer column and one count in view at 390 (n65 .23; cycle 13 n62 .57). (4) Formats: a duration in words ('12 h 30 min'), a day-and-month date with no year (`date(d, 'short')` ignores its options today), and an x tick format apart from the cursor readout's (n66 .29; n63, n64 and n66 wishes). Each field names two cases; say in the Spec what changing it after 3.0 would cost.
acceptance: A Spec with these four choices and their defaults is submitted and ruled on before code
Two cards in one row end at one height in the layout harness
Stacked panes share the card's box at 1800 and 390 with no pixel heights in app code (layout test)
A long numeric table keeps its name and answer column in view at 390 in the chosen form (layout test)
The three formats exist and are documented
out_of_scope: Behaviour fixes (v3-expr-14-kit-fixes); a Heatmap joined to another grain's focus and a BarList leader highlight (one case each); the trial scenarios.
proof: The Spec's verdict; make check; layout tests; shots of n63, n64, n65 and n66 rebuilt by nobody: the next cycle reads the fields from what ships.
